results.title: Rented GPUs got a fifth dearer in a month · Eigna
results.author: James Sherborne
highlights:
Journal 26 October 2026 3 min

# Rented GPUs got a fifth dearer in a month

In October the price of renting an H100 rose about 25% in a month, while token prices fell a quarter in four weeks. Two prices, both set by someone else.

The cost of AI has two meters, and in October they ran in opposite directions.

## Compute went up

Ornn’s index of transacted GPU rental prices settled on 26 October with an H100 at USD 3.17 an hour, up 24.8% in one month. An H200 rose 29.9% to USD 6.21, a B200 21.4% to USD 9.76. 1 1 Ornn Compute Price Index, settled 26 October 2026: H100 SXM, H200, B200 and A100, volume‑weighted transacted prices per GPU hour. One large GPU cloud raised its list prices from 1 October by 17% to 21%: an H100 from USD 3.85 to 4.50 an hour, an H200 from 4.50 to 5.40.

## Tokens went down

Ramp’s AI Index, from its own customers’ card and bill data, saw the blended price businesses pay the two largest model vendors fall to USD 0.64 per million tokens, 25.4% lower than four weeks before. Token volume rose; token spend barely moved. 2 2 Ramp AI Index, 14 October 2026, token data to the week ending 11 October; Ramp notes its sample is its own customers. Commentary: Ara Kharazian.

## What the two have in common

Neither price was set by the company paying it. In four weeks the vendors’ shares of business spend moved six points, prices moved by a fifth or more, and a rented GPU cost a quarter more than it did a month earlier. A plan built on either meter is a plan built on someone else’s pricing.

An owned model changes which costs you carry. On your own servers, with Eigna Local, the cost is the machine, its power and a fixed running fee. A meter does not appear.

...

Honesty first: Eigna Hybrid and Eigna Cloud train and run on dedicated rented GPUs in the region you choose, so these prices matter to us as well. It is one reason our prices are still marked proposed, and why we measure throughput per machine before we publish a cost per answer.

The lesson we take from October is not that renting is wrong. It is that the cost of a model you rely on every day should be one you can plan, on a model that does not change until you decide.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

Our read: This is a Compute story with a Capital ending. GPU-backed loans were underwritten on falling collateral values. If older chips keep earning, useful lives stretch and those loans look better than feared. The constraint is moving to power and memory: a Dell executive told an audience he sees about 20% more memory supply next year against roughly 200% more demand. Capacity that is already powered and running is the scarce asset, not the chip itself.

results.title: Nebius Raised Cloud GPU Prices Up to 21% — The Local Inference Math Just Shifted | GeniusTechLab
highlights:
October 26, 2026 · 7 min read · AI Hardware

Cloud GPU compute just got more expensive again. Effective October 1, 2026, Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) raised its on-demand rates across all four of its current Nvidia platforms by roughly 12–21% — the second major increase inside a year. The H100 NVLink jumped from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, the H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, and the flagship B300 now rents at $9.50 an hour. On its face it's one neocloud's price list. In reality it's the cleanest price signal yet that on-demand AI compute is being repriced as a scarce utility — and that shifts the break-even math toward hardware you own.

...

## The October 2026 rate card, line by line

Nebius publishes its list pricing openly, which makes the change easy to audit straight from the company's official price page. The on-demand, pay-as-you-go numbers that took effect October 1:

| GPU platform | Before | After (Oct 1, 2026) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 NVLink | $3.85 / GPU-hr | $4.50 / GPU-hr | ~+17% |
| H200 NVLink | $4.50 / GPU-hr | $5.40 / GPU-hr | +20% |
| B300 | ~$7.85 / GPU-hr | $9.50 / GPU-hr | ~+21% |

Read together with independent EU cloud price trackers — which put the median H200 rental up roughly 25% year-over-year — the direction is unambiguous. And note the shape of the increase: it's the spread between committed and on-demand pricing that's widening, not demand cooling. On-demand is becoming the premium product; the discount goes to whoever signs a contract.

...

Three forces are compounding. First, HBM is the binding constraint: Rubin Ultra's memory demands and the broader AI buildout have absorbed the wafer and HBM supply that would normally flow into next-gen accelerators — the same dynamic inflating the DDR5 prices on our memory crisis tracker. Second, hyperscalers are signing away future capacity in multi-year blocks, which shrinks the pool available to spot buyers. Third, grid power has become a real queue: new data-center capacity waits on substations, not chips, so even fully-funded builds land late.

For neoclouds, the choice between reprice and ration isn't really a choice. When allocation is scarce, you raise the rate for the customers who didn't commit. That's mechanically what happened on October 1 — and with enterprise inference demand still compounding quarter over quarter, the pressure is structural, not cyclical.

...

Here's the arithmetic that changed this month. An always-on H100 at $4.50/hr is about $3,240 per month, or ~$39,000 per year — before the March 2026 hike it was $27,750. That's the number small teams quietly absorbed when they "just left the instance running."

...

The bottom line: October's hike didn't change what AI costs — it changed who pays the shortage tax. Committed buyers and hardware owners are largely insulated; on-demand renters absorb the increase in full. As Rubin and MI450 supply land through 2027 most analysts expect rates to flatten, not roll back. Until then, every month of continuous on-demand inference is a month of equity you didn't build. If cloud is still your default, this is the quarter to price the alternative honestly.

results.title: H100 rental prices are spiking even as Wall Street worries about an AI bubble - Startup Fortune
results.author: Dave Barr
highlights:
Nebius hiked its H100 rate to $4.50 an hour on October 1 while CoreWeave's bond yields topped 16% the same month, showing compute scarcity and debt-fueled neocloud risk rising side by side.

...

GPU rental rates just climbed as much as 44% since December, even as bond markets panic over AI debt. Both things are true at once, and that tension is the real story.

Nebius raised its on-demand H100 rate from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on October 1, 2026, a roughly 17% jump. Runpod's Secure Cloud H100 SXM rate climbed from $3.29 in early September to $3.99 by mid-October. Across the market, Silicon Data's H100 Rental Index, launched in May 2025 as the first daily benchmark of its kind for GPU rental pricing, rose from $2 per GPU-hour on December 9, 2025, to $2.88 on October 24, 2026, a 44% increase.

That reverses a trend that had been running the other way for most of 2025, when falling H100 prices were treated as early evidence that the chip shortage was easing and the AI boom might be cooling off. It isn't cooling off. Demand for compute is outrunning supply again, badly enough that Nvidia's older H100, now superseded by both Blackwell and the shipping Vera Rubin generation, is getting more expensive to rent rather than cheaper.

Normally an older chip gets discounted as buyers migrate to newer silicon. That isn't happening here because demand is still outrunning available capacity. Nvidia has disclosed supply constraints affecting its current and future data-center systems, while Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on October 23 that AWS capacity was largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028. Demand therefore continues to spill onto H100 clusters that are already racked and running.

results.title: B200 deals top Nebius list price; only Ornn's index shows it | SecondSource
highlights:
Daily Brief Oct 26, 2026

# B200 deals top Nebius list price; only Ornn's index shows it

Source: Ornn, 2026-10-25

Correction: the October 18 issue said short GPU leases cost 2.5 to 4 times as much as long ones; that multiple is withdrawn. The multiple compared two different figures. For short leases it used CoreWeave's self-reported price of about US$40 million per MW per year. For five-year leases it used about US$10 million to US$16 million per MW per year, which SecondSource derived from total contract value. The two sides don't line up on GPU generation, capacity accounting or signing date. How much of the multiple is a term premium can't be determined.

## At a glance

1. Ornn, a company that publishes a GPU rental-price index built from completed deals, puts B200 at US$9.70 per GPU-hour, up 20.65% in a month and above the US$8.50 on-demand list price of Nebius, a cloud provider that rents out GPUs. On the same index, H100 rose only 6.32%.

...

## Today's main line

### 1. [Today] (index, October 25) On Ornn's transaction index, B200 and H200 rental prices rose more than 20% in a month and passed a provider's list price, while H100 lagged

Ornn compiles a GPU rental-price index from completed deals, and the October 25 reading shows B200 and H200 rental prices up more than 20% in a month, to above the on-demand list price of Nebius, a cloud provider that specializes in renting GPUs. H100 rental prices rose only 6.32% in a month on the same index and still sit below the Nebius list price; transaction prices so far come from Ornn alone. Our read: list price is not a ceiling on B200 and H200 rents, at least among the deals Ornn records.

Why it matters: Buyers who budget B200 and H200 rentals against provider list prices may be underestimating what completed deals now cost. H100 deals still sit below list. The evidence so far is one index, Ornn's.

# GPU Rental Rates Rise on Solid AI Demand; Supply-Demand Imbalance Persists

## AI Summary

• Amazon stated that most of its 2027 supply and a significant portion of its 2028 supply are fully booked, while SpaceX also explained that compute rental requests exceed current supply. • In October, Nebius raised on-demand prices for major GPUs by approximately +17% to +21%, notably increasing the hourly rate for the B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. • Spot Preemptible VM prices are also priced without significant discounts compared to on-demand rates, reflecting strong GPU rental demand. • It is analyzed that short-term contracts allow GPU investment costs to be recouped with one year of revenue, and that resolving the supply-demand imbalance in the short term will be difficult due to the scarcity of immediately available compute.

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
If you rent GPUs at a provider's own list rates, you are probably paying more than you did a few weeks ago. This page shows the rises we have verified on providers' own pages — each one dated — and the half of the market that has not moved yet.

### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

### Verda — three rises in four days, in full

All figures USD per GPU per hour, read on verda.com/pricing on each date shown.

| GPU | Oct 22 | Oct 23 | Oct 24 | Oct 26 | 4-day move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.34 | $4.51 | $4.56 | $4.61 | ▲ 6.2% |
| H200 | $5.66 | $5.89 | $5.95 | $6.01 | ▲ 6.2% |
| B200 | $8.07 | $8.36 | $8.44 | $8.52 | ▲ 5.6% |
| B300 | $10.28 | $10.69 | $10.80 | $10.91 | ▲ 6.1% |
| GB300 | $11.82 | $12.29 | $12.42 | $12.55 | ▲ 6.2% |
| A100 80GB | $2.07 | $2.13 | $2.15 | $2.16 | ▲ 4.3% |
| A100 40GB | $1.52 | $1.56 | $1.56 | $1.58 | ▲ 3.9% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $2.40 | $2.49 | $2.52 | $2.54 | ▲ 5.8% |
| L40S | $1.77 | $1.81 | $1.81 | $1.83 | ▲ 3.4% |

### The half that has not moved

Against those rises, the cheapest verified offers on our board did not move at all during the week of Oct 19–26:

| GPU | Best verified offer | Provider | Oct 19 → Oct 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $2.25/hr | TensorDock (8-GPU minimum) | — unchanged |
| H200 | $3.59/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| B200 | $5.98/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| RTX 4090 | $0.20/hr | nafnaf | — unchanged |
| A100 80GB | $1.09/hr | Thunder Compute | — unchanged |

Read the terms before you chase the floor — minimum commitments and community-cloud availability differ from list-rate clouds. But the fact stands: on Oct 26 you could still rent an H100 for roughly half the rate a rising list price asks ($2.25 vs $4.50–$4.61). Rising list prices have not pulled the floor up — yet.

results.title: Nvidia H200 Rental Rates Rise 160% Since January
results.author: CryptoResearch AI
highlights:
Nvidia H200 rental costs have surged roughly 160% since January 2026, leading a broad price hike across AI chips as cloud providers and spot markets struggle to match demand.

CryptoResearch AI 25 October 2026 · 1 min read

Nvidia H200 rental rates have climbed roughly 160% between January 1, 2026, and mid-October. The sharp run-up reflects an ongoing compute bottleneck, as appetite for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to outstrip available hardware.

The price pressure extends across Nvidia's broader product roster, though the H200 has posted the steepest trajectory. Year-to-date data shows B200 rental pricing up around 120%, the RTX PRO 6000 up roughly 65%, and the H100 gaining approximately 35%. Even the six-year-old A100 is commanding higher rental fees than it did at the start of January.

...

Across monitored providers, median on-demand rental rates for the H200 sit between $4.27 and $4.94 per GPU-hour. Spot platforms offer lower pricing, with hourly rates starting near $1.47 and extending to $3.88.

Hyperscalers sit at the expensive end of the spectrum. Platforms such as AWS and Azure see H200 prices averaging between roughly $7.91 and more than $10.60 an hour.

Individual cloud providers are adjusting their fees accordingly. Nebius increased its on-demand H200 rate by 20% on October 1, 2026, taking prices from $4.50 to $5.40 per GPU-hour. The company also pushed up its H100 pricing by 17% in the same update.

results.title: Nvidia H200 rental costs rise about 160% since January
results.author: Diego Almada Lopez
highlights:
Renting Nvidia's H200 now costs far more than it did at the start of 2026, and even older chips are getting pricier

 by Diego Almada Lopez 

 Sat 24 Oct 2026 · 19:19 EDT · 2 min read 

Renting an Nvidia H200 now costs about 160% more than it did at the start of the year.

The increase covers the period from January 1, 2026 through mid-October. It points to demand for AI computing power that supply still can’t match.

## The H200 leads a broad price climb

The H200 isn’t the only Nvidia chip getting more expensive to rent. It is simply getting more expensive faster than the rest of the lineup.

Here is how year-to-date rental increases compare across Nvidia’s models:

H200: up about 160%

B200: up about 120%

RTX PRO 6000: up around 65%

H100: up approximately 35%

The oddest data point belongs to the A100. That chip is six years old. It now rents for more than it did in January.

...

## What renters are actually paying

Median on-demand rental prices for the H200 sit around $4.27 to $4.94 per GPU-hour across tracked providers.

Spot marketplaces are cheaper. There, H200 rates can fall as low as about $1.47 per GPU-hour, with spot pricing ranging up to $3.88.

At the other end are the hyperscalers, the giant cloud platforms like AWS and Azure. Their H200 rates average from about $7.91 to more than $10.60 per hour.

Individual providers are also nudging prices upward. Nebius raised its on-demand H200 price from $4.50 to $5.40 per GPU-hour, a 20% increase. The change took effect on October 1, 2026.

Nebius didn’t stop at the H200. In the same adjustment, it raised H100 rates by 17%.

- Cloud hyperscalers charge up to $10.60 per H200 GPU-hour, while spot marketplaces offer rates as low as $1.47.

Spot market rates vary between $1.47 and $3.88 per hour, while major cloud hyperscalers like AWS and Azure charge between $7.91 and more than $10.60 per hour. Individual providers are raising rates as well, with Nebius increasing its on-demand H200 pricing from $4.50 to $5.40 per hour on October 1, alongside a 17% hike for H100 chips.
